transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-27
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Arcadia Head of Product), Daniel Chen (Arcadia Lead Eng), Marta Lopez (Arcadia Security), Omar Aziz, Lena Wu

Summary (auto): quick demo of hosted chat (streaming), parameter impacts, and retry playbook. Security questions on SSO/KMS and data retention. Pilot agreed — run benchmark + share docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm Sofia, i'll run the quick walkthrough and ethan will jump in on the demo bits. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya Rao: good thanks, excited to see the streaming stuff. we want low-latency answers in the mobile app.
[00:11] Ethan Park: great — we'll show streaming behavior, then params like temperature and max tokens, and finally retry/backoff patterns.
[00:18] Daniel Chen: quick context — we're running node microservices on GCP, expect bursts during promotions, and we care about p95 latency and cost per 1k queries. also security team will ask about SSO and key mgmt.
[00:30] Marta Lopez: yep — SOC2 and KMS are critical. we need audit logs and encryption at rest.
[00:36] Sofia Martinez: absolutely, we have SOC 2 docs, audit logs in the console, and KMS integrations for private deployments. i'll send the pack after the call.
[00:44] Ethan Park: ok jumping into the console — this is the hosted API view. you'll see a simple chat endpoint, live streams, and latency breakdown per token. (audio: minor typing noise)
[00:58] Ethan Park: when we talk about streaming, the key is you get tokens as they're generated which reduces perceived latency for end users. you can implement optimistic UI — start rendering partial responses.
[01:12] Priya Rao: is streaming compatible with our batching strategy? we often batch requests on the edge.
[01:16] Ethan Park: yes — Redwood does continuous batching at the runtime level; it tries to coalesce requests while still sending partial frames to clients. batching reduces cost but if you need strict tail-latency, you can set min-batch windows or pin requests to low-latency lanes.
[01:31] Daniel Chen: you said "pin to low-latency lanes" — that maps to dedicated capacity?
[01:34] Sofia Martinez: correct — design options are hosted (shared), dedicated pools, or private (VPC/on-prem). for strict SLOs dedicated is common. but for most mobile chat flows hosted with the right configs strikes the cost/latency balance.
[01:47] Omar Aziz: any rough numbers for p95 on hosted?
[01:50] Ethan Park: p95 varies by model and length. for the small/medium LLMs we've onboarded, p95 for a single-turn streaming chat was in the 120–350ms range for token generation per token, end-to-end depends on prompt size. we'll share benchmark sheet.
[02:05] Lena Wu: regarding cost — will we be charged for partial streams?
[02:09] Sofia Martinez: billing is per token consumed/returned. partial frames don't change token accounting; you pay for tokens generated. console shows token-level cost breakdown so you can correlate cost to routes.
[02:18] Priya Rao: ok, on params — what's your recommendation for temperature/top_p and max tokens for short retail assistance flows?
[02:24] Ethan Park: for deterministic product lookup, keep temperature 0–0.2, top_p around 0.8, and cap max_tokens tightly (e.g., 40–80). for creative responses you can raise temperature. also recommend a safety layer in front to normalize outputs.
[02:39] Daniel Chen: what about streaming and stop sequences — how do we ensure we don't cut off important content?
[02:44] Ethan Park: use stop tokens and also have client-side heuristics. the runtime supports structured outputs and function/tool calling which can help avoid mid-stream truncation.
[02:55] Marta Lopez: security: if we go hosted, will PII be stored? retention?
[02:59] Sofia Martinez: hosted API doesn't store customer data by default beyond short-lived logs; we support turning off retention and offer private deployments for strict data residency. will include retention config in the security doc.
[03:12] Priya Rao: good. can you explain retry/backoff patterns? our engineers are worried about double-processing payments-like events.
[03:19] Ethan Park: yes — two parts: idempotency and backoff. for chat you typically use an idempotency key on the conversation ID, and on client you implement exponential backoff with jitter. the runtime supports automatic retries for transient errors and you can configure max attempts and fallback model.
[03:34] Daniel Chen: how do you handle partial responses on retry — will the user see duplicate tokens?
[03:38] Ethan Park: the SDK can resume from the last acked token; best practice is server-side checkpoints or transactional saves of last token index so the client can continue or request a restart. we demoed a resume path earlier in a different call.
[03:52] Priya Rao: what about KV cache or prefix caching? we want to reuse context for repeated requests.
[03:56] Ethan Park: we have prefix caching and KV cache — it reduces token compute. for retail product details you can cache product embeddings or prompt prefixes and reduce cost significantly. caching plays well with streaming.
[04:09] Sofia Martinez: i'll note to share a short doc on caching recommendations tuned for retail.
[04:13] Omar Aziz: any limits on streaming connection length? mobile clients can drop.
[04:16] Ethan Park: we support reconnect + resume in the SDK; if a connection drops, client can reconnect and resume using conversation state. short-lived KV cache per session is recommended.
[04:28] Daniel Chen: can we test a small pilot — e.g., 1k messages across a sample conversation set to see latency and cost?
[04:32] Sofia Martinez: yes — that's exactly what we propose. ethan will run a benchmark and we'll share raw numbers.
[04:36] Ethan Park: action: i'll run a 1k-message streaming run against a small sample from you and capture p50/p95/p99 and token counts.
[04:42] Priya Rao: timeline?
[04:44] Ethan Park: plan for results in ~1 week. hoping to have numbers by 2025-03-05.
[04:49] Marta Lopez: and how do we get SOC2 docs?
[04:52] Sofia Martinez: i'll email the pack by 2025-03-03, includes audit logs, retention settings, and KMS notes for private option.
[04:58] Daniel Chen: any tricky gotchas migrating from our current endpoint?
[05:02] Ethan Park: common items: idempotency keys, adapting to streaming events, and tuning batch windows. we can share a migration checklist.
[05:09] Priya Rao: great, should we also check a dedicated pool option if p95 from hosted looks too high?
[05:13] Sofia Martinez: yes — if pilot shows tail latencies above your SLO, we can discuss a brief dedicated trial. dedicated has predictable throughput and lower variance.
[05:21] Priya Rao: ok that sounds reasonable.
[05:24] Sofia Martinez: quick recap of next steps: 1) Sofia sends security pack by 3/3, 2) Ethan runs streaming benchmark by 3/5 and shares results, 3) Priya/Daniel share dataset and peak TPS by 3/3, 4) schedule 30m pilot kickoff next week.
[05:41] Daniel Chen: noted. thanks everyone.
[05:44] Priya Rao: thanks, helpful session.
[05:46] Ethan Park: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links to console traces and benchmark results.
[05:51] Sofia Martinez: bye!

(End of transcript)
